brief: DB's year-end outlook: a broadening economic recovery, as manufacturing ISM rebounded and cyclical hiring picked up, combined with AI demand and Iran-war-driven commodity prices to produce an unprecedented S&P 500 earnings boom, growth accelerating from 25% in Q1 2026 to 34% in Q2, with AI beneficiaries and the rest of the index contributing almost equally. DB raised its 2026 EPS forecast to $358 (28% growth) and 2027 to $420 (17% growth). Earnings have historically anchored equities through political and geopolitical shocks, a 1960s parallel, but the S&P 500 is currently 15% below the level year-end earnings imply and its forward multiple is 19.1x, near cycle lows, because positioning is cautious and priced for only about 10% growth. DB's demand-supply framework, positioning plus inflows plus buybacks net of issuance, supports a year-end target of 8000 with upside risk. Catalysts: Q3 earnings season, rates rising on real-rate and growth normalization with bond shorts crowded near extremes, and midterms where Republicans are expected to lose about 40 House seats even as Q4 has rallied in 21 of the last 23 midterm years. Sector calls: overweight Tech, Financials, Industrials, Metals and Mining, Healthcare and data center and industrial REITs, neutral Energy, underweight most defensives.
